Reviewed 2026-09-29: official biography, own biography, first speech and public employer statements. Targeted queries for Slater join date and public-service department supplied 2024 and court role but no department or full-time terms. No login-restricted professional content accessed.

Identity checked against Menzies candidacy and employer statements. UK Better Society Capital/Shearman solicitor and overseas architects or namesakes are not this verified record. Matt Gregg's 2019 start belongs to Gregg, not Ng.
Year-level 2024–2025 is not one exact year; no boundaries or FTE inferred. The frozen roster's empty occupation list is not zero career experience. Initial partial record; last follow-up 2026-09-29.

2026-10-02 follow-up identified Home Affairs protection-visa decision-making from30October2025 Hansard, with27August2025 confirmation of multiple departments. Re-inspected employer material names union delegate and Fitzroy Legal Service/local kindergarten volunteering. Targeted court/department searches did not establish dates or hours. December2023 LawLife case notes by Gabriel Ng and September2024 Law Institute Journal admission list are new leads requiring identity corroboration; not employment evidence by themselves. Next: Pillay associate lists, departmental annual reports/public CV and Slater appointment terms. Do not treat last job rhetoric as an exact chronology or infer Services Australia employment from policy discussion. Totals remain unknown.

2026-10-03 follow-up corroborated Ng's entry to the Victorian legal profession: the Law Institute of Victoria's September2024 admissions list records Gabriel Ng as admitted on24July2024. Identity is supported by the unusual exact name, jurisdiction and year matching Slater and Gordon's identified Menzies candidate and2024 lawyer appointment. This is used only as a dated professional milestone, not a Slater start date, full-time-hours proxy or evidence of continuous work; graduate/pre-admission employment remains possible. Searches of County Court, legal databases and public profiles did not disclose Judge Pillay associate boundaries or departmental dates. LawLife's December2023 case note remains an uncorroborated same-name lead and is not used as employment evidence.

2026-10-04 follow-up materially narrows the Home Affairs chronology: first-person parliamentary remarks on 4 February 2026 say Ng was a CPSU delegate at Home Affairs and, towards the end of his time there, was present after the Albanese government took office when Clare O'Neil announced TIS jobs would be brought in-house. This supports Home Affairs employment continuing after May2022 and resolves the delegate's union identity, but it does not justify a start/end date, full-time status, leave or separate union employment. Exact-name County Court/Pillay searches returned no associate boundaries. LawLife case notes dated17–18December2023 remain same-name evidence consistent with court/legal work but still lack enough identity/employer metadata to treat as a job boundary. Next: County Court personnel/annual-report records, departmental appointment records, and Slater appointment terms.
